cultural.vision_reason: This flat greenstone amulet with a schematic linear face (bar eyebrows/nose, incised mouth, single suspension hole) matches the well-known Mezcala (Mesoamerican) stone mask/pendant tradition, not Khmer stone or metal ornament styles — no Khmer parallel exists for this form.

physical.title: amulet; figure
physical.summary: A pendant or amulet made of stone, depicting a stylised human face. The face has angular featuresand narrow eyes. The back is flat and smooth and the top right corner has a hole from which the object may have originally hung. There is no hol;e in the top left, although this may have been lost or worn away, possibly in antiquity, as the left side of the figure is uneven.

cultural.vision_reason: This is Chinese porcelain painted in Germany with a chinoiserie scene—it has no connection to Khmer culture at all; it is not jewelry, and it depicts a European fantasy of a Chinese subject, not anything Khmer people made or used.

physical.title: cup
physical.summary: Chinese porcelain cup and saucer, painted in Germany. The cup is of deep beaker shape with flared rim and the saucer has curved sides. Both pieces are plain white and each is marked with a beribboned lozenge in a double ring in underglaze blue. They are painted in red and gold with an elaborate chinoiserie scene which shows on the saucer a large figure with conical hat holding an umbrella, with a smaller one behind him, both standing on a decorative pedestal, flanked by two other figures with fancy hats, seated and kneeling on brackets formed by the surrounding scrollwork, which contains perched birds and formal fruit motifs. The cup is matchingly painted with a similar pair of figures standing in conversation, two others standing singly, and a figure kneeling, with a fan, among similar scrollwork.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a bronze/copper aeolipile (fire-blower) depicting an African male head, an Afro-Portuguese/West African trade object type, not a Khmer artifact or jewelry item; nothing in the piece connects it to Cambodia or Khmer culture.

physical.title: fire-blower
physical.summary: Hollow embossed bust made from copper sheet of an African male; puffed out cheeks; hole between pursed lips; hole in base; holes in lobes of ears; one ear-ring remains; lid with hinge on top of head;  a fire-blower aeolipile.Traces of black patination and gilding.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a Roman-style mould-made terracotta oil lamp with a maker's stamp (LVCCPOLY, a Latin name), a classic Roman volute lamp form — not a Khmer object, and not jewelry at all.

physical.title: lamp
physical.summary: Mould-made pottery lamp with a wide rounded shoulder decorated with relief tongues and impressed ovules, and a simple moulded rim surrounding the plain discus. The broad nozzle has a rounded tip and pseudo-double-ended volutes, between which is an air-hole. At the rear is a ring-handle. Across the slightly raised base is the impressed name LVCCPOLY. Covered with a matt orange slip.
